memory_update.text: LOPE is the primary reference candidate for online program management and university-services infrastructure because its disclosed business is directly tied to university shared services, online/hybrid programs, and healthcare education expansion.

STRA should remain in the underfollowed lane as a workforce-education and employer-benefits infrastructure candidate, especially if ETS, Workforce Edge, Sophia Learning, and employer-affiliated enrollment continue to grow.

COUR is a small-cap underfollowed platform candidate for university and enterprise credential infrastructure, but it needs post-merger verification of segment quality, degree economics, and institutional retention.

LRN is a second-order candidate rather than a pure university OPM name; keep it only if the research scope includes career learning and scalable online education infrastructure beyond higher education.

Need a later Layer 1C/2 search for less obvious suppliers to these companies: enrollment analytics, CRM, student-success software, state authorization compliance, instructional design tools, simulation technology, marketing/enrollment agencies, and higher-ed regulatory compliance vendors.
